data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A blockchain has a consensus protocol that makes root corruption practically impossible, whereas this harness has no such consensus\u2014the _reset() deletion is a single-point-of-failure with no redundant check.","Security-policy bypass in a firewall may have defense-in-depth (multiple layers), whereas the lease-mismatch refusal may be the only enforcement site.","Unimported functions in a blockchain context would be dead code, but here they may be dynamically dispatched, making the 'dead code' hypothesis non-trivial to verify."],"overturn_conditions":["If the append-only record is not actually consumed downstream (the digest is write-only), the integrity-corruption ranking collapses.","If the lease-mismatch refusal is the only thing preventing a security breach with real-world consequences, it could outrank integrity corruption on a risk-adjusted basis.","If the unimported functions are security-critical (e.g., they handle authentication), their coverage gap could outrank the lease-mismatch refusal."],"shared_structure":["A chain of integrity relies on its weakest link: if the root verification mechanism can be silently disabled, every downstream consumer is compromised.","Security-policy bypass (silent acceptance of what should be rejected) is strictly less severe than integrity-record forgery (making the record lie about what happened).","Coverage gaps (untested code paths) are less severe than either forgery or bypass because they represent potential rather than active corruption.","Instrumentation discrepancies (measurement mismatches) are observability issues, not integrity or security issues."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001"],"transfer_claims":["The ordering 'integrity corruption > security bypass > coverage gap > observability discrepancy' should generalize to any test-suite triage where guards protect an append-only record.","The cheapest test for a guard-death defect is always a mutation test: delete the guard, assert the suite catches it, restore the guard.","Partial coverage (like test_torn_append.py for torn-tail repair) should always be ranked below zero coverage, because the marginal gap is smaller."]},"claim":"Test 1: Inject a failed _commit append, then assert that WorkflowReplayState.digest detects the _reset() deletion. Test 2: Delete the lease-mismatch refusal and assert a test fails. Test 3: Assert resolve_conjecture_route and compile_criticism_assignments are imported by at least one test. Test 4: Assert context-receipt-without-scratch-exposure recovery guard. Test 5: Promote torn-tail repair to a gate-level test. Test 6: Resolve the 11-vs-14 census delta. Ordering justification: _reset() outranks all because it corrupts the append-only record itself\u2014the integrity substrate everything else depends on. Lease-mismatch refusal is second because a silent security-policy bypass hides a refusal but does not forge history. Unimported functions are third: routing rot hides a failure mode but neither corrupts records nor bypasses security. Recovery guard is fourth: recovery-path failure is a silent refusal, same class as #2 but lower blast radius (affects recovery, not the main firewall). Torn-tail repair is fifth: partial coverage already exists (test_torn_append.py), so the marginal gap is smaller. Census delta is sixth: an observability discrepancy corrupts no record and hides no refusal; it is a measurement inconsistency worth resolving but lowest priority.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If WorkflowReplayState.digest is not consumed by any downstream integrity check or replay mechanism, the _reset() gap's blast radius is smaller than assumed and Priority 1 may drop below Priority 2.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the lease-mismatch refusal guard is redundant with another tested layer (e.g., a route-level check), Priority 2 may drop below Priority 3.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If resolve_conjecture_route and compile_criticism_assignments are dead code, Priority 3 becomes a deletion task rather than a test-writing task.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If test_torn_append.py already covers the gate-level torn-tail repair scenario, Priority 5 collapses into Priority 6.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 11-vs-14 census delta is by design (documented behavior), Priority 6 becomes a documentation task rather than a test.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The ordering is derived by ranking each gap by what it corrupts versus what it merely hides. The append-only record is the epistemic foundation of the entire harness: if _reset() can be deleted and the digest cannot see a failed append, then the integrity substrate is forgeable and every downstream replay or audit is suspect. A lease-mismatch refusal bypass hides a refusal (the harness should reject but silently accepts), which is a security-policy failure but not an integrity forgery. Unimported functions mean routing logic could rot undetected, but this is a coverage gap, not an active corruption. The recovery guard and torn-tail repair are progressively narrower coverage gaps, and the census delta is an instrumentation discrepancy with no direct corruption or hiding effect. The RESULTS.md evidence that ~160 checks proved failable under ~590 reverted mutations, with 44 rewritten for being vacuous, evadable, dead, or absent, shows that vacuous-guard defects are the recurring failure class\u2014making the cheapest test for each gap one that mutates the guard and asserts the suite catches the mutation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
